newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil police kill eight in prison revolt.
newsitem.headline: Brazil police kill eight in prison revolt.

text.p: Brazilian police killed eight prisoners during a jail revolt in what church officials on Thursday condemned as a "massacre."

A spokeswoman for the government of the northeastern state of Paraiba said prisoners rebelled at the Roger Penitentiary in the state capital Joao Pessoa on Tuesday evening and eight were killed when special military police units were sent in.
"The prisoners were holding the prison governor hostage and threatening to kill him," the spokeswoman said, adding that the dead were all shot.
The Archdiocese of Paraiba condemned the police action, saying it was reminiscent of 1992 when police killed 111 inmates at Carandiru prison in Sao Paulo state during a riot.
"It was a massacre. Most of the prisoners only had kitchen knives and no serious attempt was made to negotiate," said Roman Catholic priest Antonio Maria Guerin.
The police action was unacceptable. We condemn crime ... but we think human rights must be respected," Guerin told Reuters from Joao Pessoa.

Paraiba officials said the police action became unavoidable after the rebellious inmates, numbering about 15, threatened to kill their six hostages, among them prison director Givaldo Farias and three guards. The rest were inmates.
Farias and two guards were injured by stray bullets during the police operation but their lives were not in danger.
In the last six months Brazil has been struck by a rash of prison rebellions, sparked by overcrowded conditions and, in some cases, the brutality of the guards.
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso last month announced plans to build 52 new jails by 1999 to ease overcrowding.
